_provenance.note: Stages 4 and 5 retired (docs/adr/0004). No 3R HIGH/CRITICAL, political MEDIUM, Stage 3 source_diversity 0.54 > 0.4, so no Stage 5 re-enable. Stage 3 located eleven primary records the brief had reached only through secondary reporting (two Hansards, two NRES parliamentary answers, RTM, UKAS, Sarawak JPN, KLH Indonesia, Polri, Singapore MSE, KLK). Nine of the eleven were re-opened in this session and quoted below; the two Hansard PDFs are image scans and are relied on through Stage 3's reading, attributed as such.

headline: Sarawak haze hit API 475. The haze law Cabinet backed in 2020 was dropped in 2023.
context: Smoke carried in from Kalimantan pushed Serian to an Air Pollutant Index of 475 on 31 August. Cabinet backed a Transboundary Haze Act in principle in February 2020; the next Cabinet decided against it in July 2020, and in November 2023 the government said it would not continue.

cards.big: Serian hit an API of 475 on 31 August; 591 Sarawak schools shut. Putrajaya once had a haze law on the table. It dropped it in 2023.
cards.sub: Cabinet backed a Transboundary Haze Act in principle in February 2020. The next Cabinet said no in July 2020. In November 2023 Parliament heard it would not continue.

cards.big: Serian recorded an API of 475 on 31 August; Kuching 407 the next morning. Above 300 is hazardous; schools shut at 200 or above.
cards.sub: Sarawak shut 591 schools on 20 and 21 August, 197,323 pupils. Health Ministry surveillance logged respiratory infections more than double in a week, 1,637 to 3,674.

cards.big: Perikatan Nasional's Cabinet said no to the Act in July 2020. In November 2023 the Pakatan Harapan-led government told Parliament it would not continue.
cards.sub: Days later it said the door stayed open. Both cited one obstacle: maps, coordinates and land records hard to get on secrecy and sovereignty grounds.

cards.big: Singapore has had an extraterritorial haze law since 2014. Its record: legal notices to six Indonesian firms, four still open in 2021.
cards.sub: Indonesia has 335 concession firms under strict oversight and 89 named suspects as of 30 August. In 2019 it sealed part of a KLK estate after a fire KLK confirmed.

cards.big: On 30 August Sarawak counted nine hotspots; Kalimantan 1,180. The absence of a Malaysian haze law is Putrajaya's own choice, made under two governments.
It is like a town that keeps drafting a fire code, files it away when the neighbour's field burns, then measures how far the smoke spreads before calling an emergency.
cards.sub: The emergency line is API 500. Malaysia has declared three haze emergencies in 29 years: Sarawak 1997, Selangor 2005, Johor 2013.

cards.big: A haze law would not put out Indonesia's fires; Putrajaya said so in 2023. Its point was to tell Malaysian planters abroad the smoke follows them home. Two governments declined to say it.

revisions: CORRECTED (Stage 3): hook sub / fact-Legal 'dropped for good on 6 November 2023' → 'would not continue' with 'three days later it said the door stayed open'. NRES parliamentary answer 9 Nov 2023 (ID 2442, oral, to Suhaili Abdul Rahman): 'Kerajaan juga tidak menolak sebarang cadangan ... termasuklah keperluan Akta Pencemaran Jerebu Merentas Sempadan'. Re-opened and quoted in this session.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): '6 November 2023 written reply' → oral parliamentary answer. NRES answer ID 2428 is labelled Lisan (oral), question 33, Tan Hong Pin (Bakri). Re-opened in this session. The word 'written' no longer appears on any card.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'Perikatan Nasional shelved it that August' → 'decided against the Act in July 2020'. Dewan Rakyat Hansard 3 Aug 2020 (repositori.parlimen.gov.my DR-03082020.pdf) records a Cabinet decision of 24 July 2020 not to proceed, announced 3 August. PDF is an image scan; relied on through Stage 3's reading, corroborated by the Malaysian Bar's 7 Aug 2020 release quoting the 3 Aug statement.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'A Pakatan Harapan-led Cabinet dropped it' → 'the Pakatan Harapan-led government told Parliament it would not continue'. The 2023 record is a ministry answer stating the government's position, not a documented Cabinet decision; the 2020 record is. The cards now distinguish the two mechanisms, and the view says 'two governments', not 'two Cabinets'.

CORRECTED (Stage 3 + Stage 2): 'from 21 August' → 'on 20 and 21 August'. RTM 20 Aug 2026 (berita.rtm.gov.my, '591 sekolah di Sarawak ditutup akibat jerebu'): 509 primary / 107,590 pupils, 82 secondary / 89,733, closed 'berkuat kuasa serta merta' for Thursday 20 and Friday 21 August. Re-opened in this session.

REPHRASED (Stage 2 bias + Stage 3): 'land records a neighbour keeps secret' → 'maps, coordinates and land records hard to obtain on confidentiality and sovereignty grounds'. NRES answer 6 Nov 2023: 'peta lokasi, koordinat, maklumat pemilik tanah dan syarikat' ... 'kerahsiaan, keselamatan dan kedaulatan negara ... sukar diperoleh'. Re-opened and quoted in this session. 'Both cited the same obstacle' rests on Stage 3's reading of the 3 Aug 2020 Hansard (landowner information, maps, coordinates; security and sovereignty) plus the 2023 answer.

CORRECTED (Stage 3) + REPHRASED (Stage 2 omission): Singapore 'has never produced a conviction' → 'Its record: notices to six Indonesian firms, four still open in 2021'. Singapore MSE written PQ reply 13 Sep 2021: six companies served legal notices under the THPA after 2015, two cases closed on the information provided, four remain under investigation; no prosecution or conviction mentioned. Re-opened in this session. The universal negative is gone; the enforcement record Stage 2 said was omitted is now the card.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): '335 concession holders with hotspots inside their licences' → '335 concession firms under strict oversight'. KLH Indonesia 22 Aug 2026: 'pengawasan ketat kepada 335 perusahaan pemegang konsesi di wilayah Sumatera dan Kalimantan'. Re-opened and quoted in this session.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): '72 arrests by 21 August' → '89 suspects named by 30 August'. Polri (tribratanews) 1 Sep 2026: 89 tersangka, 189 laporan polisi, per Brig-Gen M. Irhamni ('kurang lebih tersangkanya ada 89 per Sabtu kemarin', i.e. Saturday 30 August). Re-opened in this session. 'Suspects named', not 'arrests'.

CORRECTED (Stage 3): 'sealed land where Malaysian parent KLK confirmed a fire' → 'sealed part of a KLK unit's estate after a fire the company confirmed'. KLK press release 14 Sep 2019 (klk.com.my PDF): 2.8 ha burned at PT Adei Plantation, 4.25 ha sealed for investigation, cause under investigation. Relied on through Stage 3's reading; the PDF is image-only in this session. 'Part of' reflects 4.25 ha of an estate; no claim of deliberate burning.
CORRECTED (Stage 3) + REPHRASED (Stage 2 unverified-detail): context 'in the region's worst haze episode since 2015' deleted. Al Jazeera characterisation with no ASMC or DOE ranking behind it.

REPHRASED (Stage 3 misleading-framing): reframe 'The smoke is Kalimantan's. The choice to meet it with letters rather than law was made in Putrajaya, twice, by both sides of the aisle.' → 'On 30 August Sarawak counted nine hotspots; Kalimantan 1,180. The absence of a Malaysian haze law is Putrajaya's own choice, made under two governments.' Removes exclusive source attribution (UKAS 31 Aug records both Sarawak and Kalimantan hotspots), removes the letters-versus-law binary (the 2023 answer lists diplomacy, AATHP cooperation, G2G work and Indonesia's peat and One Map initiatives), and replaces 'both sides of the aisle' with 'two governments' (PN 2020; PH-led unity 2023). Hotspot counts: UKAS 31 Aug 2026, 29–30 Aug window, re-opened in this session. Rhetorical family: re-anchored number + value restructuring.

REPHRASED (Stage 3 misleading-framing): analogy sub 'It has been crossed three times in 29 years: Kuching in 1997, Selangor in 2005, Johor in 2013' → 'Malaysia has declared three haze emergencies in 29 years: Sarawak 1997, Selangor 2005, Johor 2013'. NRES media archive 23 Jun 2013 (ID 126): highest API ever recorded was Sarawak 1997 at 860; Port Klang and Kuala Selangor under haze emergency in 2005 when API surged above 500; Muar and Ledang 2013 with Muar at 746. Re-opened in this session. Episodes, not threshold crossings; Sarawak, not Kuching alone.

REPHRASED (Stage 3 unverified counterfactual): view 'The Transboundary Haze Act would not have put out Kalimantan's fires' → 'A haze law would not put out Indonesia's fires; Putrajaya said so in 2023'. The 6 Nov 2023 answer's position is that legislation alone would not resolve transboundary haze (Stage 3 reading; consistent with the alternatives list re-opened in this session). 'Its point was to tell Malaysian planters abroad' frames the reach as the proposal's stated purpose (Yeo Bee Yin, Hansard 7 Jun 2023 per Stage 3; FMT 5 Oct 2023), not as enacted scope.

REPHRASED (Stage 3): context 'Smoke from Kalimantan fires pushed Serian' → 'Smoke carried in from Kalimantan pushed Serian'. UKAS 31 Aug 2026 quotes Uggah: 'angin membawa jerebu ke Sarawak dari arah Kalimantan'. No exclusivity claim.
REPHRASED (Stage 3): 'Health Ministry sentinel clinics' → 'Health Ministry sentinel surveillance' (58 clinics plus 18 hospital outpatient departments; KKM via Bernama 27 Aug 2026).
REPHRASED (Stage 3): 'schools close at 200' → 'schools close at 200 or above' (Sarawak JPN 1 Sep 2026 per Stage 3; consistent with NADMA portal 12–13 Aug 2026 in the brief).

REPHRASED (Stage 3 unverified timestamps): hook and fact-Environmental drop '10 am' and any 'peak' wording; '475 on 31 August' stands on UKAS 31 Aug 2026 (re-opened) and DOE APIMS via The Star and DayakDaily. 'Kuching 407 the next morning' stands on RTM 1 Sep 2026 (8 am) per Stage 3 and The Star 1 Sep.

INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified): 'The next Cabinet said no in July 2020' (hook sub). Same fact as the Legal card's 'decided against the Act in July 2020', Hansard 3 Aug 2020 per Stage 3 plus Malaysian Bar 7 Aug 2020.
INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified): 'Three days later it said the door stayed open' (fact-Legal sub). 6 Nov to 9 Nov 2023, both NRES parliamentary answers, both re-opened and quoted in this session.

INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified): 'nine hotspots; Kalimantan 1,180' (reframe). UKAS 31 Aug 2026: Sarawak 9, Kalimantan 1,180 for 29–30 Aug; also The Star 30 Aug citing ASMC (1,180 / 9). Two independent chains.
INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified): 'Its record: notices to six Indonesian firms, four still open in 2021' (fact-Regional). Singapore MSE 13 Sep 2021, re-opened in this session.

INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified): 'Putrajaya said so in 2023' (view). NRES answer 6 Nov 2023 as read by Stage 3: legislation alone insufficient; re-opened answer lists non-legislative measures as the government's approach. Attribution kept deliberately general ('Putrajaya') because the record is a ministry answer, not a Cabinet decision.

REJECTED (Stage 2 fix wording): Stage 2 proposed 'land records protected by a neighbour's sovereignty and confidentiality laws'. Not adopted: the ministry answer speaks of confidentiality, security and sovereignty considerations, not of identified neighbouring statutes. Used the ministry's own framing instead.
REJECTED (Stage 2 fix wording): Stage 2 proposed 'one of the region's worst haze episodes since 2015'. Not adopted: still a comparative ranking with no primary series behind it. Deleted instead.

NOT APPLIED (Stage 3 corrections to non-card material): asthma 61→219 (not 61→158), 2005 emergency declared 11 Aug 2005 (not 1 Aug), Shahwahid 2016 is an EEPSEA research report giving RM1.49 bn (not RM1.74 bn peer-reviewed), July 2026 burn area 94,545.49 ha per Kementerian Kehutanan via Polri. None of these figures is on a card; all are corrected in the brief's CONTRADICTIONS and SOURCES sections.

INTRODUCED (Stage 6 self-verified, length pass): trimmed to the 180/220/300 budget without dropping qualifiers: hook big 'its own haze law' → 'a haze law'; fact-Environmental 'sentinel surveillance' → 'Health Ministry surveillance' (still the ministry's sentinel count, not a census); fact-Legal 'decided against' → 'said no to', 'Three days later' → 'Days later' (6 to 9 Nov 2023), 'hard to obtain' → 'hard to get'; fact-Regional 'The counter-argument is real:' dropped as framing scaffolding, 'named 89 suspects by 30 August' → '89 named suspects as of 30 August'. Every specific re-checked against the same sources as before the trim.

synthesis_notes: OVER-INTEGRATION CHECK: Stage 2 (bias 15) and Stage 3 (accuracy 62) pointed the same way on every shared flag (school date, 'keeps secret', Singapore enforcement record, 'worst since 2015'), so no averaging was needed. Where they differed in remedy (Stage 2 offered softer replacement wordings for 'keeps secret' and 'worst since 2015'), the primary record was followed rather than either reviewer's phrasing. STAGE 2 vs STAGE 3 on Singapore: Stage 2 logged 'never produced a conviction' as VERIFIED via a Greenpeace statement; Stage 3 marked it UNVERIFIED because a 2021 record cannot prove a negative through 2026. Stage 3 is right; the card now states the documented enforcement record rather than the negative. HEADLINE: 'was dropped in 2023' retained. The 6 Nov 2023 answer says the government 'tidak akan meneruskan' the proposal, which is a drop; what was removed is 'for good', because the 9 Nov answer kept the option open, and the Legal card now carries that qualifier. COMPRESSION: analogy sub uses state names (Selangor 2005, Johor 2013) for Port Klang/Kuala Selangor and Muar/Ledang to fit the 300 combined cap; the state names are true and the brief carries the localities. 'Sarawak 1997' replaces 'Kuching 1997' per Stage 3. FRAMING: the political record is now asymmetric on purpose, because the records are: one documented Cabinet decision (PN, July 2020) and one ministry position (PH-led unity government, Nov 2023, door left open). Cards say 'Cabinet' for 2020 and 'government' for 2023; the view says 'two governments'. LENGTH: all cards within the 180/220/300 budget; context 271. SR 80: the factual spine survived intact, but fourteen wording corrections were needed, three of them (school date, 'written', 'for good') outright errors that Stage 1 should have caught from the primary record. LENGTH PASS: final combined lengths hook 131+166=297; fact/Environmental 127+164=291; fact/Legal 152+148=300; fact/Regional 134+163=297; reframe 152+0=152; analogy 167+129=296; view 187+0=187; context 278; headline 82. Legal sub compresses 'kerahsiaan, keselamatan dan kedaulatan' to 'secrecy and sovereignty grounds' (security dropped for length; all three are the ministry's own words). Regional sub says 'a KLK estate' for the PT Adei Plantation subsidiary estate.
